lines.caption: This is a tour of pull request 102, which adds two options to open a new Thunar window at a set size, place and workspace.
lines.say: This is a tour of pull request one oh two, which adds two options to open a new Thunar window at a set size, place and workspace.

lines.caption: It has three parts: what this PR adds, how it was built and verified, and what comes later.
Part 1. What this PR adds.
You run thunar with -g for the size and place, and -s for the workspace, counting from 1.
lines.say: You run Thunar with dash g for the size and place, and dash s for the workspace, counting from one.

lines.caption: Still in your own process, the values of -g and -s are passed on untouched, even after -T.
lines.say: Still in your own process, the values of dash g and dash s are passed on untouched, even after dash capital T.

lines.caption: The running Thunar parses them once; a bad value prints an error, and the window still opens.
lines.say: The running Thunar parses them once; a bad value prints an error, and the window still opens.

lines.caption: The options wait in a queue beside the files the command opens, so they belong to this command alone.
They are applied only when Thunar creates a new window; a tab in a window you already have ignores them.
The window gets its size, then its place; placing works on X11, and on Wayland only the size applies.
lines.say: The window gets its size, then its place; placing works on X eleven, and on Wayland only the size applies.

lines.caption: The workspace is set as the window first appears, so it lands there and your view doesn't move.
The size from -g isn't saved as your remembered size; resizing by hand still saves as before.
lines.say: The size from dash g isn't saved as your remembered size; resizing by hand still saves as before.

lines.caption: Until now Thunar always opened at your last size, on the workspace you were on, so scripts couldn't lay out windows.
The key fact: the thunar you type usually hands its options to a running Thunar, so they must travel with the command.
lines.say: The key fact: the Thunar you type usually hands its options to a running Thunar, so they must travel with the command.

lines.caption: Without the pass-through, a value after -T would be taken as a right-pane folder; grouped flags like -gs count too.
lines.say: Without the pass-through, a value after dash capital T would be taken as a right-pane folder; grouped flags like dash g s count too.

lines.caption: It accepts width by height, a position, both, and offsets from the right and bottom edges.
Each queued file carries its own options, action and --window flag, so a Ctrl+N window or another command never gets them.
lines.say: Each queued file carries its own options, action and dash dash window flag, so a control N window or another command never gets them.

lines.caption: A window with options appears only once its folder, split view and tabs are set up; a tab instead says they were ignored.
A place-only -g un-maximizes the window first, so a remembered maximized state can't override it.
lines.say: A place-only dash g un-maximizes the window first, so a remembered maximized state can't override it.

lines.caption: GTK deletes the workspace property just before showing the window, so a one-shot handler sets it at map, with a fallback.
Its resizes go unsaved while it's still off screen, or when they repeat its last size; the first new size after it appears saves.
This table sums it up: a size, a position, both, or a corner measured from the right and bottom edges.
-s 2 opens on workspace 2; a bad value prints an error and opens normally on the current workspace.
lines.say: Dash s two opens on workspace two; a bad value prints an error and opens normally on the current workspace.

lines.caption: With no new window, both are ignored and the command says so; on Wayland, only the size applies.
With split view and tabs, the window is at least the asked size, and appears once both panes are set up.
The issue suggested a GTK call that only messages the window manager, which xfwm4 ignores before the window is on screen.
lines.say: The issue suggested a GTK call that only messages the window manager, which X F W M four ignores before the window is on screen.

lines.caption: So the PR sets the workspace property itself, after GTK has cleared it, and sends the suggested call as a fallback.
The PR changes three Thunar source files, and adds a test, this page and its narration.
To undo it, revert this PR; nothing new is stored in settings.
Part 2. How it was built and verified.
It follows the two issues' lists, GTK's own geometry rules, and the merged tabs options from PR 92.
In this session's cloud container it built and installed, and the smoke test and 12 earlier tests passed, before CI's review.
The new test opened windows at the asked size, at a set corner, and 40 pixels from the bottom-right, within 2 pixels.
The remembered width stayed the same until a resize by hand; a bad geometry printed its error and still opened.
-s 2 opened on workspace 2 while the view stayed on 1; a bad workspace printed its error; help lists both.
lines.say: Dash s two opened on workspace two while the view stayed on one; a bad workspace printed its error; help lists both.

lines.caption: That test passed in 23 seconds, after fixing only the test script itself.
A new test case, -g with split view and tabs, passed in the local run of the R21 fix.
lines.say: A new test case, dash g with split view and tabs, passed in the local run of the R twenty-one fix.

lines.caption: Not run: a tab in a window you already have, the no-flash promise frame by frame, and Wayland.
CI's latest run, of the fixes from its first two reviews, built the PR and passed every test.
Locally, the tree with the R21 fix built, installed, and passed the smoke test and all 13 tests.
lines.say: Locally, the tree with the R twenty-one fix built, installed, and passed the smoke test and all thirteen tests.

lines.caption: CI's sixth review covered the fix for R31, R32 and R34; its build and tests are still running.
lines.say: C I's sixth review covered the fix for R thirty-one, R thirty-two and R thirty-four; its build and tests are still running.

lines.caption: The screenshots haven't been audited yet; that happens on CI's shots.
A fresh review agent, at level high, found five things; four were fixed and one was kept.
The big ones: the workspace was being wiped before the window appeared, and a shrunk size could have been saved.
Two small ones: options could reach another window, and grouped flags lost their values after -T.
lines.say: Two small ones: options could reach another window, and grouped flags lost their values after dash capital T.

lines.caption: Kept: offsets from the right and bottom use the default size, just as GTK's own parser does.
CI reviewed it six times, at level high, and found 38 things, R1 to R38.
lines.say: C I reviewed it six times, at level high, and found thirty-eight things, R one to R thirty-eight.

lines.caption: CI's fixes: a place-only -g un-maximizes, no workspaces is handled, numbers fit X's range, and the test waits first.
lines.say: CI's fixes: a place-only dash g un-maximizes, no workspaces is handled, numbers fit X's range, and the test waits first.

lines.caption: A hand resize lost in the first five seconds, and options swapped between commands, were each fixed in two steps.
Options are now passed as a parameter, and a fallback request moves the window to its workspace.
When a setting turns the open into a tab, -g and -s are still ignored, as the issues ask, but now it says so.
lines.say: When a setting turns the open into a tab, dash g and dash s are still ignored, as the issues ask, but now it says so.

lines.caption: The sixth review found only two small things in the latest fix; its build and tests are still running.
One commit fixed the second review's findings: one queue entry per file, and a size guard with no timer.
CI fixed four from the third review itself, including a crash risk when a second command arrives while files open.
R21 is accepted by the owner's decision: CI's re-check agent never reported, a bug tracked in issue 103.
lines.say: R twenty-one is accepted by the owner's decision: C I's re-check agent never reported, a bug tracked in issue one oh three.

lines.caption: The fourth review found two more: a later command's files took the earlier one's settings, and one error dropped them all.
Five small, unconfirmed findings from that review were accepted, each with a short reason given here.
The fifth review found a new-window flag one command could leave for the next; that and two small ones were fixed.
Three more small, unconfirmed findings were accepted: two of them predate this PR.
Two small findings from the sixth review were accepted too: an unused flag, and a refactor idea.
Unconfirmed findings are closed by naming them in the fix commits, or accepted when low and from a later review.
CI's build and tests of the latest fix are still running; the screenshot check follows them.
After the merge, try it on your own desktop, with your real workspaces.
The pull request, its CI comments, CI's review and test runs, and both issues are linked here.
Part 3. What comes later: nothing depends on it yet.
No open issue builds on these options, so merging this PR unblocks nothing else.
One follow-up, issue 103, makes CI's review wait for its checking agents.
lines.say: One follow-up, issue one oh three, makes C I's review wait for its checking agents.

lines.caption: In short: one command can now open a Thunar window at the size, place and workspace you choose, and you stay put.
